sources.citation: Jackson, Suzannah J. 2015. Indigenous Sign Language of Far North Queensland. Learning Communities: International Journal of Learning in Social Contexts (Special Issue: Indigenous Sign Languages) 16: 92-99. doi:10.18793/lcj2015.16.07
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Read in full (pp. 92-99): sociolinguistic overview of ISL among Deaf Indigenous signers of Cairns/Cape York/Torres Strait, its origins in Australian Aboriginal Sign Languages and Torres Strait signed languages, interview excerpts and a few sign comparisons (woman, toilet, sister, nephew/niece). No phonology, prosody, stress or prominence discussion of any kind; a signed language, so word stress is not an applicable category.
